chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a woman whose husband died and had not consummated marriage with her; he said:
She must not marry until she observes a waiting period of four months and ten days, the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the legally prescribed duration of the widow's waiting period
key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: a woman whose husband has died
key_terms.تُوُفِّيَ: passed away; used here for the death of the husband
key_terms.عِدَّةَ: the waiting period mandated in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Does a woman whose husband dies before consummation still have to observe the widow's 'iddah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a widow must observe the prescribed 'iddah of four months and ten days even if her husband died before consummating the marriage. It establishes that the waiting period for death applies by virtue of the husband's death itself, not only after consummation.
